docs.title: Cobblemon Defeated Catch Chance
docs.text:
Not released yet

Defeated Catch Chance has no public download yet. These pages describe the current development build, 0.0.1. Anything not described here is not in the mod yet.

docs.title: Cobblemon Defeated Catch Chance
docs.text:
Beat it, then catch it. In Cobblemon a wild Pokémon you knock out is gone the moment the battle ends. With this mod it stays down for a moment, asleep and on its last HP, and one good throw can still bring it home.

There is nothing to learn. Install it and win a wild battle. (Operators can tune it, and turn each part off.)

MC 1.21.1 Fabric NeoForge Not released yet Cobblemon 1.8+

Get started How it works

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• 💤 It stays down: a wild Pokémon a player beats lies on the ground, asleep at 1 HP, instead of vanishing.
  • ⏱️ One last chance: 60 seconds by default to throw a Poké Ball at it, and everyone nearby is told it is down.
  • 🎯 Easy odds: asleep and on 1 HP, it is as easy to catch as Cobblemon's capture formula allows.
  • 🏃 A miss wakes it: it sprints away from you, fades out and is gone. Balls thrown at it while it runs catch nothing.
  • 🚫 No rematch: a downed Pokémon can be caught, never battled again.
  • 💾 Survives a restart: the window keeps counting through a save and reload.
  • 🔧 Commands & Config: the window's length, the flee's length, and an on/off switch for each, in game.

docs.title: Commands & Config
docs.text: The mod needs no setup. Everything here is for operators who want to change the defaults.

docs.title: The config file
docs.text:
config/cobblemon_defeated_catch_chance.json is written the first time the mod runs and holds every setting:

{
  "window": {
    "enabled": true,
    "window_seconds": 60
  },
  "flee": {
    "enabled": true,
    "flee_ticks": 60
  }
}
Setting Default Range What it does window.enabled true Off: a beaten wild Pokémon vanishes as in plain Cobblemon, with no window. A Pokémon already in its window finishes it. window.window_seconds 60 5 to 3,600 How long a beaten Pokémon stays down and catchable, in seconds. flee.enabled true Off: a missed ball does not wake the Pokémon; it vanishes in a puff within a few seconds. flee.flee_ticks 60 1 to 1,200 How long the run before it vanishes lasts, in ticks (20 ticks = 1 second).

A missing value takes its default, and one out of range is pulled to the nearest end of its range. The file is written back whole each time the mod reads or changes it, so every setting is always in it.

A file that is not valid JSON

The mod logs a warning, runs on the defaults and leaves the file as it is. Changes made with /dcc config are then not saved until the file is fixed and the server restarted.

docs.title: /dcc config
docs.text:
Operators only (permission level 2). Every change applies at once, on a live server, and is saved to the file.

Command What it does /dcc config Lists both features, whether each is on, and each setting (with its default when it differs). /dcc config <window\|flee> Lists one feature. /dcc config <window\|flee> enabled <true\|false> Switches a whole feature on or off. /dcc config window window_seconds <5-3600> Sets the window's length, in seconds. /dcc config flee flee_ticks <1-1200> Sets the run's length, in ticks. /dcc config <window\|flee> reset Puts the feature back to its defaults and switches it on.

The command takes numbers only inside each setting's range. A value outside it is refused by the command itself.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Defeated Catch Chance targets Minecraft 1.21.1 on Fabric and NeoForge, with Cobblemon 1.8. Cobblemon 1.7.x is not supported: the mod refuses to load on it.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Dependency Notes Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric Loader 0.17.2 or newer, or NeoForge 21.1 or newer the jar for your loader Fabric Language Kotlin or Kotlin for Forge the one for your loader (Kotlin for Forge 5 or newer) Architectury API both loaders Cobblemon 1.8 or newer

There are no optional mods to add.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Install Cobblemon and the libraries for your loader.
  2. Drop the Defeated Catch Chance jar for your loader into mods/. Never put both loaders' jars in.
  3. On a server, install it on the server and on every player's game: the fade-out of a fleeing Pokémon is drawn by the player's own game.
  4. Win a battle against a wild Pokémon. It lies down instead of vanishing: throw a ball.

That is the whole setup. The mod writes config/cobblemon_defeated_catch_chance.json the first time it runs; you only touch it to change the defaults.

docs.title: With Cobblemon Nuzlocke
docs.text: Cobblemon Nuzlocke carries its own copy of this feature. While that copy is present, this mod stands down and logs that it did, so the two never run together and never double a body.

docs.title: The window
docs.text:
A wild Pokémon that a player beats in battle does not vanish when the battle ends. Instead:

  1. The moment it faints it is kept alive at 1 HP so the end of the battle cannot remove it.
  2. When the battle is over, it is put back on its feet at 1 HP, frozen in place, silent, and laid down asleep. Smoke rises from it.
  3. Everyone within 48 blocks sees a message above their hotbar: "Pikachu is down — 60s to catch it!" (with the Pokémon's name and the window's length). It is also in Spanish for players on es_es.
  4. The countdown starts at that moment, when the body appears, not when the Pokémon fainted.

While the window is open the Pokémon does not move, make a sound or wake up. You can walk up to it and throw a ball.

Only a player's win counts

The window opens for wild Pokémon beaten in a battle that a player won. A Pokémon that was never in a battle with a player is left to Cobblemon as usual.

docs.title: Why it is easy to catch
docs.text: The window puts the Pokémon to sleep (the status, not just the pose) and pins it at 1 HP. Cobblemon's capture formula reads exactly those two things, so a downed Pokémon is as easy to catch as the formula allows. Your ball, your Pokémon's level and the Pokémon's catch rate still count as always.

docs.title: Catching it
docs.text: Throw any Poké Ball. A successful catch ends the window and the Pokémon goes to your party or PC through Cobblemon's normal capture flow.

docs.title: A missed ball
docs.text:
With the flee on (it is by default), a ball that fails changes what happens next:

  1. The Pokémon breaks free of the ball.
  2. It wakes up, cries, and sprints away from the thrower.
  3. It fades out over flee_ticks (60 ticks, about 3 seconds by default) and is gone.
  4. Balls thrown at it while it runs catch nothing. The chance is over.

With the flee off, a failed ball just lets the Pokémon go: it vanishes in a puff within a few seconds, after the ball's break-free animation.

docs.title: When time runs out
docs.text: If the window ends with no catch, the Pokémon vanishes in a puff of cloud and a short sound.

docs.title: No rematch
docs.text: A downed Pokémon cannot enter a battle again, and neither can one that is running away. It can only be caught.

docs.title: A save and reload
docs.text:
The end of the window is stored on the Pokémon as an absolute world time, so the window keeps counting through a server restart or a chunk unload, and picks up again when the Pokémon loads.

A Pokémon that was running away when the server stopped is removed rather than saved mid-flee.

docs.title: What it does not do
docs.text:
• It does not give a second battle, extra experience or any reward: only the chance to catch.
  • It does not touch Pokémon that were not wild, or battles between players.
  • It does not change Cobblemon's capture formula.

Every part can be switched off in Commands & Config.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Common surprises, what causes them, and what to do. If yours is not here, post it in the Discord: it files the ticket for you.

docs.title: The mod does not load
docs.text: Defeated Catch Chance needs Cobblemon 1.8 or newer. On 1.7.x it refuses to load with a dependency error. Check too that you put in the jar for your loader, and its Kotlin and Architectury libraries. See Getting Started.

docs.title: A beaten Pokémon still vanishes
docs.text:
• Did a player win? The window opens only for a wild Pokémon beaten in a battle a player won.
  • Is it switched on? Check /dcc config window: with enabled off, beaten Pokémon vanish as in plain Cobblemon.
  • Is Cobblemon Nuzlocke installed? While Nuzlocke has its own copy of this feature this mod stands down, and the server log says so. The window you see is then Nuzlocke's, with Nuzlocke's rules.

docs.title: The window is shorter or longer than 60 seconds
docs.text: It follows window.window_seconds, and the message above the hotbar says the exact number. The countdown starts when the Pokémon lies down, after the battle, not at the knockout. See Commands & Config.

docs.title: My ball did nothing on a Pokémon that was running
docs.text: That is the rule: a missed ball wakes the Pokémon, and from then on balls thrown at it catch nothing. Switch the flee off with /dcc config flee enabled false if you would rather it just vanish.

docs.title: My config changes do not stick
docs.text: If the config file is not valid JSON the mod keeps it untouched and runs on the defaults, so nothing is saved. The log has a warning with the file's path. Fix the file and restart.

docs.title: I want a Pokémon to stay down longer
docs.text: Raise window.window_seconds (up to 3,600). Anything longer is not supported.
